[[File:Hubble s law.jpg|thumbnail|As can be seen, galaxies appear to move away from earth at a velocity roughly proportional to their distance from earth]]
The '''Hubble-Lemaître law''' states:

# Galaxies appear to move away from earth,
# The velocity of recession ($v$) is roughly proportional to distance ($d$) from earth, i.e.,

$$
v=H_0d
$$
where $H_0$ is the '''Hubble's constant'''. Its value varies with the rate of expansion of the universe over time. Today, $H_0 \approx 70 \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$, where $\mathrm{Mpc}$ denotes megaparsec ( $10^6$ [[parsec]]).

The Hubble's constant can be calculated via the [[1st Friedmann equation]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q2563}}</ref><ref>{{#cite:Q2573}}</ref>

== History ==

The Hubble-Lemaître law was first predicted by Belgium astrophysicist and priest [[Person:Georges Lemaître|Georges Lemaître]] towards 1927 and experimentally verified by [[Person:Edwin Hubble|Edwin Hubble]] in 1929. The exact value of the '''Hubble constant($H_0$)''' has been subjected to much scientific debate ever since.
